message.content: The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) was a small, probably insectivorous mammal that lived roughly 70–80 million years ago, at the base of the Laurasiatherian clade. This ancestor would have resembled a tiny, shrew‑like animal and represents the point where the lineages that eventually led to the modern carnivores (including cats) and the odd‑toed ungulates (including horses, rhinos, and zebras) began to diverge.
